Certainly! Below are some sample entries for a comprehensive MLA Works Cited list. Please note that MLA (Modern Language Association) style is commonly used for papers and citation in the humanities. The 8th edition of the MLA Handbook, published in 2016, introduced a new model for entries in the Works Cited list, emphasizing the concept of "containers" and focusing on a set of core elements.

Here are some examples:

**Book by a single author:**
Smith, John. *The Art of Fiction*. Penguin Books, 2015.

**Book by two authors:**
Doe, Jane, and Richard Roe. *The Science of Writing*. Oxford UP, 2017.

**Book by three or more authors:**
Brown, James, et al. *The Craft of Poetry*. Cambridge UP, 2018.

**Chapter or section in an edited book:**
Johnson, Mary. "The Role of Imagination." *The Creative Mind*, edited by Susan White, Harvard UP, 2016, pp. 45-60.

**Article in a scholarly journal:**
Williams, Anna. "The Impact of Digital Media on Modern Literature." *Journal of Digital Humanities*, vol. 10, no. 2, 2019, pp. 123-135.

**Article in a magazine:**
Thompson, Mark. "The Future of Reading." *The Atlantic*, vol. 323, no. 4, Apr. 2019, pp. 56-60.

**Article in a newspaper:**
Lee, Jennifer. "New Library Opens in Downtown Area." *The New York Times*, 15 Mar. 2019, p. A4.

**Website:**
"MLA Formatting and Style Guide." *The Purdue OWL*, Purdue U Writing Lab, 2019, owl.purdue.edu/owl/research_and_citation/mla_style/mla_formatting_and_style_guide/mla_general_format.html.

**Online article from a database:**
Garcia, Maria. "The Evolution of the Novel." *Literary Review*, vol. 12, no. 3, 2018, pp. 45-60. *JSTOR*, doi:10.2307/123456789.

**Film or movie:**
*The Matrix*. Directed by Lana and Lilly Wachowski, performances by Keanu Reeves, Laurence Fishburne, and Carrie-Anne Moss, Warner Bros., 1999.

**Television series episode:**
"Ozymandias." *Breaking Bad*, created by Vince Gilligan, performance by Bryan Cranston, season 5, episode 14, AMC, 15 Sept. 2013.

**Lecture or speech:**
King, Martin Luther, Jr. "I Have a Dream." Address. March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom, 28 Aug. 1963, Lincoln Memorial, Washington, D.C.

**Interview:**
Jones, Sarah. Personal interview. 10 Apr. 2019.

**Email:**
Doe, Jane. "Re: Writing Tips." Received by John Smith, 20 Mar. 2019.

**Social media post:**
@RealWriter. "Just finished the first draft of my novel! #amwriting #writerslife." *Twitter*, 15 Mar. 2019, twitter.com/RealWriter/status/123456789.

**Image from a website:**
Van Gogh, Vincent. *Starry Night*. 1889. Museum of Modern Art, New York. *MoMA*, www.moma.org/collection/works/79802.

**Podcast:**
"Episode 42: The Art of Storytelling." *The Writing Life*, narrated by Jane Doe, 15 Mar. 2019, writinglife.libsyn.com/episode-42-the-art-of-storytelling.

**E-book:**
Austen, Jane. *Pride and Prejudice*. 1813. Project Gutenberg, 2008, www.gutenberg.org/files/1342/1342-h/1342-h.htm.

**Government publication:**
United States, Department of Health and Human Services. *Mental Health: A Report of the Surgeon General*. U.S. Government Printing Office, 1999.

Remember to alphabetize the entries by the author's last name or by the title if there is no author. Also, note that the MLA Handbook suggests using hanging indents for each entry, where the first line is flush with the left margin and subsequent lines are indented.

Here is a comprehensive example of a Works Cited list in MLA format for various types of sources:

Book
Smith, John Doe. Title of the Book. City of Publication: Publisher, Year of Publication. Medium of Publication.

Example:
Smith, John Doe. The Awesome Book. New York: Penguin Random House, 2021. Print.

Journal Article
Author's Last name, Author's First Name. "Article Title." Journal Title Volume Number.Issue Number (Year of Publication): Pages. Database Name. Date of Access. Web.

Example:
Doe, Jane. "The Importance of Reading for Kids." Childhood Education 56.9 (2020): 48-52. Academic Search Complete. 30 Mar. 2021. Web.

Website Article
Author's Last name, Author's First Name. "Article Title." Title of the Website. Website Name, Day Month Year of Publication, URL.

Example:
Doe, Jane. "The Benefits of Physical Activity." Health.gov, 15 Jan. 2021, https://www.health.gov/articles/the-benefits-of-physical-activity.

Website with No Author
Title of the Article. Title of the Website, Day Month Year of Publication, URL.

Example:
"What Is the Water Cycle?" Earth Science, World Book, 15 Jan. 2021, https://www.worldbook.com/article/X736199.

Website with No Author and No Date
Title of the Article. Title of the Website. URL.

Example:
"The History of Basketball." NBA.com. https://www.nba.com/history/history_of_basketball.

E-book
Author's Last name, Author's First Name. Title of the Book. Version. Publisher, Year of Publication. Ebook Collection. Web. Date of access.

Example:
Doe, John. The Digital Revolution. 1st ed. Wiley, 2020. Ebook Collection (EBSCOhost). 30 Mar. 2021. Web.

Social Media
Author's Username. "Post Title." Social Media Platform, Day Month Year, Time of Post.

Example:
@JohnDoe. "Having a great day in the park!" Twitter, 15 Jan. 2021, 10:00 AM.

Interview
Interviewee's Last name, Interviewee's First Name. Interview by Interviewer's Last name, Interviewer's First Name. Title (if given), Day Month Year, Location.

Example:
Rodriguez, Maria. Interview by Jane Doe. "How to Run a Successful Small Business," 15 Jan. 2021, New York City.

---

This sample includes a variety of sources such as novels, short story collections, anthologies, translations, and books by well-known authors. Each entry follows the standard MLA format for citations.

Here are samples for a Comprehensive MLA Works Cited list, including books, articles, and websites:

Books:

Smith, John. The Great Gatsby. Scribner, 1925.

James, Henry. The Ambassadors. Scribner, 1903.

Articles:

Hollander, Renee. "The Influence of F. Scott Fitzgerald's The Great Gatsby on American Culture." American Literature, vol. 83, no. 1, 2011, pp. 73-91. JSTOR, www.jstor.org/stable/41480005.

Websites:

Fitzgerald, F. Scott. "The Great Gatsby." Literature Resource Center, Gale, 2019. Literature Resource Center, link.galegroup.com/apps/doc/PP3139330482/LitRC?u=broward21711&xthc=gale_primary_search&sid=LitRC&xid=4ab398a9. Accessed 15 Mar. 2023.

"The Great Gatsby." SparkNotes, SparkNotes LLC, www.sparknotes.com/lit/gatsby/. Accessed 15 Mar. 2023.
